Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 28, verse 4:

As Pharaoh schemed against the Children of Israel: ﴿He slaughtered their sons and spared their women﴾

Out of fear that there would emerge among them one through whom his kingdom would end, God, glory be to Him, outwitted him by bringing forth this infant, raising him in Pharaoh's own house and in his lap, until there befell him what he had been dreading, as it has been said:

*"When you fear a matter that has been decreed, and you flee from it, you find yourself heading straight towards it."*

(Section)

God's scheming, glory be to Him, does not fall outside two categories.

The first: that God, glory be to Him, performs an act beyond the power of the one against whom He schemes, so that the scheme is pure decree (qadar), not a matter of the Law (shar'). Such is His scheming against those who disbelieved, when He took vengeance upon them with various kinds of punishment. Likewise was the story of Yusuf, peace be upon him: Yusuf could do no more than place the drinking-cup in his brother's saddlebag and send a caller who called out: ﴿O caravan, you are surely thieves﴾ [Yusuf: 70]. When they denied it, he said: ﴿What is the penalty for it, if you are liars?﴾ They said: ﴿Its penalty is that he in whose bag it is found shall himself be its recompense﴾ [Yusuf: 74–75].

That is, the penalty is that the one who stole becomes enslaved to the owner of what was stolen, either absolutely or for a set period.

This was the law of the family of Ya'qub, peace be upon him.

The second: that He inspires him with a permissible matter, or a recommended one, or an obligatory one, which brings him to the good objective. Accordingly, His inspiring Yusuf, peace be upon him, to do what he did is itself a part of His scheming, glory be to Him. Thus He has schemed for him in both kinds of scheming. This is why He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿We raise in degrees whom We will﴾ [Yusuf: 76].

In this there is an indication that precise knowledge of subtle stratagems that lead to a lawful objective which God and His Messenger love, such as supporting His religion, breaking its enemies, granting victory to the truth and suppressing the falsifier, is a praiseworthy attribute by which God raises the servant's rank, just as knowledge by which one defeats the falsifier and refutes his argument is a praiseworthy attribute by which He raises the rank of His servant. As He, glory be to Him, said in the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and his debate with his people and the breaking of their argument:

﴿And that was Our argument, which We gave to Ibrahim against his people. We raise in degrees whom We will﴾ [al-An'am: 83].

On this basis, there is a scheming which is lawful, but it is not the scheming by which forbidden things are made permissible and obligations are dropped. That is a scheming against God and His religion, and God and His religion are the ones being schemed against in this category. It is impossible that God, glory be to Him, would legislate this kind of scheming.

Furthermore, this scheming is not accomplished except by an act intended for a purpose other than its lawful purpose, and it is impossible that God, the Exalted, would legislate for a servant to intend by his act what God has not legislated that act for.

(Benefit)

His wisdom has required that the robes of victory and its rewards are poured out only upon those who are broken and humbled. ﴿And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land, and to make them leaders and make them the inheritors, and to establish them firmly in the land, and to show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts from them that which they had been fearing.﴾

(Benefit)

His wisdom has required that the robes of victory and its rewards are poured out only upon those who are broken and humbled. ﴿And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land, and to make them leaders and make them the inheritors, and to establish them firmly in the land, and to show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts from them that which they had been fearing.﴾

(Fa'ida)

Ten realities pertain only to the non-existent (ma'dum): the condition (shart) and its consequence (jaza'), the command (amr), the prohibition (nahy), supplication (du'a'), promise (wa'd), threat (wa'id), hope (taraji), wishing (tamanni), and permissibility (ibaha).

[Section: The Station of Trust in God, Most High]

Among the stations of "You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help" (Iyyaka na'budu wa-iyyaka nasta'in) is the station of trust (thiqa) in God, Most High.

The author of "al-Manazil" (Sahib al-Manazil) said:

Trust (al-thiqa) is the blackness of the eye of reliance (tawakkul), the point at the center of the circle of delegation (tafwid), and the pupil of the heart of submission (taslim).

He opened the chapter with the words of God, Most High, to the mother of Moses: ﴿And when you fear for him, cast him into the river, and do not fear nor grieve﴾ [al-Qasas: 7].

Her act here is precisely her trust in God, Most High, for had it not been for the perfection of her trust in her Lord, she would not have cast her child and the piece of her liver into the current of the water, its waves toying with him and its flow carrying him to wherever it ends or stops.

His meaning is that trust is the essence and kernel of reliance, just as the blackness of the eye is the most noble part of the eye.

By saying that it is the point of the circle of delegation, he indicated that the axis of reliance turns upon it, and it lies at its center in the manner of a point in a circle. The point is the center around which the circumference revolves, the directions of the circumference relate to it equally, and every part of the circumference faces it. Likewise, trust is the point around which delegation revolves.

Similarly his saying: the pupil of the heart of submission. The most noble part of the heart is its pupil (suwayda'), which is the vital core by which life exists, and it lies at its center. Hence, if delegation were the heart, trust would be its pupil; if it were the eye, trust would be its blackness; and if it were a circle, trust would be its point.

It has already been mentioned that many people interpret reliance (tawakkul) as trust, and make it its reality. Others interpret it as delegation, and others as submission.

So I know that the station of reliance comprises all of that.

Thus, in the view of the Shaykh, trust is the spirit, and reliance is the body that carries it; its relation to reliance is like the relation of excellence (ihsan) to faith (iman). And God knows best.

[Section: The Degrees of Trust in God, Most High]

He said: It has three degrees. The first degree: the degree of despair (iyas).

This is the servant's despair of opposing the decrees (muqawamat al-ahkam), so that he refrains from disputing the divisions (munaza'at al-aqsam), in order to be freed from the impudence of initiative (qihat al-iqdam).

Meaning: the one who trusts in God, by his belief that when God Most High issues a judgment and decrees a matter, there is no turning back from His decree and no one can overturn His ruling. Whoever God has decreed for, with a portion of provision, or obedience, or a state, or knowledge, or otherwise, it must come to him. And whoever God has not allotted this to has no way to it whatsoever, just as he has no way to fly to the sky or carry mountains. By this measure he refrains from disputing the divisions: what is his of them will come to him despite his weakness, and what is not his of them he will never attain by his strength.

The difference between his saying "opposing the decrees" and "disputing the divisions" is that opposing the decrees is that his will attaches to the very thing that is in God's judgment and decree. When his will attaches to that, he contends with creation over the divisions and disputes with them concerning them.

His saying "is freed from the impudence of initiative" means: through trust in God he is freed from this impudence and audacity, which is taking the initiative toward what has not been decreed for him and not allotted to him.

And God, glorified is He, knows best.

[Section: The Second Degree: The Degree of Security (amn)]

He said: The second degree is the degree of security: the servant's security from the loss of what has been decreed and the annulment of what has been inscribed.

Then he attains the spirit of contentment (rawh al-rida), and if not, then the eye of certainty (ayn al-yaqin), and if not, then the gentleness of patience (lutf al-sabr).

He says: whoever attains the aforementioned despair attains security. That is because whoever realizes the knowledge of God, and that what God has decreed has absolutely no turning back, is secure from losing his allotted portion that God has apportioned to him. He is also secure from any shortfall in what God has written for him and inscribed in the Book that is inscribed. Thus he attains the spirit of contentment, that is, its ease, pleasure, and bliss; for the one who is content is in ease, pleasure, and joy.

As in the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

"Indeed God, in His justice and equity, placed the spirit and joy in certainty and contentment, and placed worry and grief in doubt and displeasure."

If the servant is unable to attain the spirit of contentment, he attains the eye of certainty, which is the strength of faith and its direct contact with the heart, such that between him and direct vision there remains only the lifting of the veil that prevents the eye from direct encounter.

If he does not attain this station, he obtains the gentleness of patience and what it contains of a good outcome. As in the well-known report: "If you are able to act for God with contentment together with certainty, then do so. If you are not able, then in patience over what the self dislikes there is much good."

[Section: The Third Degree: Witnessing the Eternity of the Truth (mu'aynat azaliyyat al-haqq)]

He said: The third degree is witnessing the eternity of the Truth, so as to be freed from the trials of intentions, the burdens of protections, and the detours upon the paths of means.

His saying "witnessing the eternity of the Truth" means: whenever his heart witnesses the Lord, glorified and exalted, as singular in eternity, he is absorbed in it from seeking, because of his certainty of the Lord, Most High's, being done with destinies, the precedence of eternity over them, and the establishment of their judgment there. Thus he is freed from the trials that present themselves to him instead of the goal. He is also freed from his deviation and turning aside, and from holding back his mount on the roads of causes by which he seeks his objectives.

This is not absolute. The paths of means are of two kinds: means that lead to the very eye of contentment. Deviation toward them, in knowledge, action, state, and preference, is pure servitude. But he should not make all his deviation upon them, such that by them he forgets the end to which they are means.

As for his freedom from the burdens of protections, it is his freedom from seeking what God, Most High, has protected him from by decree. He does not burden himself to seek what has been withheld from him.

Another aspect: that by witnessing the precedence of eternity, he is freed from the burdens of his precautions and the intensity of his guarding against hardships, knowing the precedence of eternity over what has been written for him of them.

So there is no benefit in burdening oneself with guarding. Yes, he guards against what he has been forbidden and what does not benefit him on his path and does not help him reach the goal.

Ibn al-Qayyim, *al-Tafsir al-Qayyim*, on Surah 28, verse 8:

As for the *lam al-'aqibah* (the lam of consequence, which they also call the *lam al-sayrurah*, the lam of outcome), as in ﴿so that it would become for them an enemy﴾, it is in reality the *lam kay* (the lam of purpose). However, it is connected to the predicate in order to indicate the intention of the one about whom the statement is made and his will. Yet it is connected to the will of the true doer of the action, who is God, glorified and exalted. That is, God did that so that such-and-such would happen. Similarly, their saying "he manumitted him so that he would die" does not mean that he manumitted him with the purpose of death. The lam is not connected to the act itself. Rather, the meaning is that God decreed that he would be manumitted so that he would die. So it is connected to what has been decreed and to God's action.

A parallel to this is the [weak] hadith: "Indeed I forget so that I may establish the sunnah" (*innī ansā li-aslunn*).

Whoever narrates it as *unassā* (with shaddah) has uncovered the veil of the meaning.

I heard our shaykh Abu al-Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah say: It is impossible for the *lam al-'aqibah* to enter the act of God. Wherever it appears in speech, it indicates either the agent's ignorance of the consequence of his act, such as the picking up of Moses by the family of Pharaoh, for they did not know its outcome, or the agent's inability to avert the consequence, as in the verse of the poet:

*Give birth for death, and build for ruin*

But as for the act of one from whom not even the weight of an atom escapes, and who is capable of all things, it can never be anything but the *lam kay* (the lam of purpose), which is the *lam al-ta'lil* (the lam of causation).

Such benefits, which are hardly found in books, require sitting with the shaykhs and scholars.

(Section)

The fifth principle: He, glorified is He, is wise. He does nothing in vain, nor without meaning and benefit. His wisdom is the intended end of the act. Rather, His acts, glorified is He, proceed from perfect wisdom for the sake of which He acts, just as they arise from causes through which He acts. His speech and the speech of His Messenger have indicated this, and this occurs in places too numerous to count, and it is not possible to enumerate all of them. So we will mention some of their types.

The first type: the explicit mention of the word *hikmah* (wisdom) and its derivatives, such as His saying: ﴿a far-reaching wisdom﴾

And His saying: ﴿And God has sent down to you the Book and the wisdom﴾

And His saying: ﴿Whoever is given wisdom has indeed been given much good﴾

*Hikmah* is beneficial knowledge and righteous action. It is called *hikmah* because knowledge and action have each attached themselves to what they concern and have reached their ends. Likewise, speech is not *hikmah* unless it leads to praiseworthy ends and beneficial objectives, guiding to beneficial knowledge and righteous action, so that the sought goal is achieved. If the speaker did not intend the benefit of his addressees, nor their guidance, nor their leading to their happiness, nor pointing them to its causes and its obstacles, and if that was not the intended goal sought, nor the purpose for which he spoke, nor the purpose for which He sent the messengers and revealed the books, nor the purpose for which He established reward and punishment, then he would not be wise, nor would his speech be *hikmah*, let alone *bālighah* (far-reaching).

The second type: His reporting that He did such-and-such for such-and-such a reason, and that He commanded such-and-such for such-and-such a reason. Such as His saying: ﴿That you may know that God knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾

And His saying: ﴿God is the One who created seven heavens and of the earth their like. The command descends among them, that you may know that God is over all things competent and that God has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾

And He said: ﴿God made the Kaʿbah, the Sacred House, a means of support for the people, and the sacred month, and the offerings and the garlands. That is so that you may know that God knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and that God is Knower of all things﴾

And His saying: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good tidings and as warners, so that people will have no argument against God after the messengers﴾

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you﴾

And His saying: ﴿So that the People of the Book may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of God﴾

And His saying: ﴿And We did not make the qiblah that you used to face except that We might know who follows the Messenger from who turns back on his heels﴾

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He sends before him and behind him guards, so that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾. That is, that they may be enabled, through this protection and watch, to convey His messages, so God knows that as actually happening. And His saying: ﴿And He sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you thereby and remove from you the defilement of Satan and to strengthen your hearts and plant firmly thereby your feet﴾. And His saying: ﴿and to nullify falsehood﴾

And His saying: ﴿And God did not make it except as good news for you and so that your hearts would be assured thereby﴾

And His saying: ﴿Say, "The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth to strengthen those who believe﴾

And His saying: ﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels, and We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve, so that those who were given the Scripture will be certain and those who believe will increase in faith﴾

And His saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced nation, that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾. And His saying: ﴿And We revealed to you the Reminder that you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them﴾. And His saying: ﴿This is a notification for the people, that they may be warned thereby and that they may know that He is but one God, and that those of understanding may be reminded﴾. And His saying: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences and sent down with them the Book and the balance that the people may maintain justice. And We sent down iron, in which is great military might and benefits for the people, and that God may make evident who supports Him and His messengers unseen﴾. And His saying: ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth that he might be among the certain﴾. And His saying: ﴿And the horses, mules, and donkeys [He created] for you to ride and as adornment. And He creates that which you do not know﴾. And this is in the Qur'an.

If it is said: The *lam* in all of this is the *lam al-'aqibah*, as in His saying: ﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾

And His saying: ﴿And thus We tested some of them by means of others, that they would say, "Are these the ones upon whom God has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾. And His saying: ﴿that He may make what Satan throws a trial for those in whose hearts is disease﴾

And His saying: ﴿that whoever perishes [would perish] upon evidence and whoever lives [would live] upon evidence﴾

And His saying: ﴿and that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline toward it, and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may commit what they are committing﴾

The answer is that what follows the *lam* in these is not the sought goal. Rather, since the act terminates in it, and it is the consequence of the act, the *lam* of causation has entered upon it, though in reality it is the *lam al-'aqibah*.

The answer comes in two ways.

The first: The *lam al-'aqibah* occurs only with regard to one who is either ignorant or unable to avert the consequence. The first is like His saying: ﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾. The second is like the saying of the poet:

*Give birth for death, and build for ruin; for all of you will pass on to perishing.*

As for one who is all-knowing of everything and capable of everything, it is impossible for this *lam* to apply to him. Rather, the *lam* in His acts and His rulings is the *lam* of wisdom and the sought goal.

The second answer: Addressing each of those places separately. As for His saying: ﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾, it is the causation (*ta'lil*) of God's decree of his being picked up and His predetermination of it. Their picking him up was only by His decree and predetermination. He, glorified is He, predetermined that and decreed it, so that it would become for them an enemy and a grief. He mentioned their act rather than His decree because it is more forceful in making it a grief and a regret for them. For one who chooses to take what will be his destruction at their hands, when he is struck by it, is greater in his sorrow, distress, and regret than one who has no part in it and no choice. He, glorified is He, wished to make manifest to Pharaoh and his people, and to others among His creation, His perfect power, knowledge, and overwhelming wisdom, and that this child whom Pharaoh had ordered slaughtered out of fear would be the one whom Pharaoh's household, by their own choice and will, would raise in their house and home, and would be in their grasp and under their control. So mentioning their act of taking him in this context is more forceful and more astonishing than mentioning the decree and predestination, though God has informed us that all the acts of His servants occur by His decree and predestination.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We tested some of them by means of others, that they would say, "Are these the ones upon whom God has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾, there is no doubt that this is the causation of the act mentioned, which is the testing of some of His creation by others, just as He tested the nobles and the eminent by means of slaves, the weak, and clients.

When the noble and the master see that the slave, the weak, and the poor man has embraced Islam, he is offended and disdainful that he should embrace it along with him or after him, and he says: "This one precedes me to good and success, and I lag behind. If that were good and happiness, these people would not have preceded us to it." So this statement from them is one part of the wisdom and the sought goal of this trial, for this statement indicates arrogance and pride and refusal to submit to the truth after complete knowledge of it. And this, though it is a cause, is sought for something else. Final causes are sometimes sought for themselves and sometimes sought for other things, and so they become a means to something sought for its own sake. The statement of these people, and what follows from that statement, necessitates effects that are sought by the Agent: the manifestation of His justice, wisdom, might, dominance, and sovereignty, and His giving to whom deserves His giving and places it appropriately, and His withholding from whom deserves withholding and whom no one else suits. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is not God most knowing of the grateful?﴾

Those who recognize the value of the blessing and thank the Benefactor for the favor He has bestowed upon them, distinguished from those who do not recognize it and do not thank their Lord for it. The trial of some by means of others occurred so that this distinction would take place, which resulted in the gratitude of some and the disbelief of others.

(Lataifah)

The knowledge of Moses' prophethood and the faith of Asiya had preceded, so his cradle (tabut) came to her house before him. A child without a mother came to a woman without a child.
Meaning: empty of everything except Musa, because of the intensity of her love for him and the attachment of her heart to him.

(Section)

As for the cosmic (kawni) prohibition, it is like His saying: ﴿And We had forbidden the wet-nurses to him before that﴾

And His saying: ﴿He said, "It is forbidden to them for forty years"﴾

And His saying: ﴿And there is a prohibition upon a town which We have destroyed, that they shall not return﴾

As for the legislative (dini) prohibition, it is like His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you are your mothers﴾ and ﴿Prohibited to you is carrion﴾; and ﴿And the game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in the state of ihram﴾

﴿And Allah has permitted trade and forbidden usury﴾.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 28, verse 14:

Al-Hasan said: "Whoever worships Allah well in his old age, Allah will grant him wisdom in his advanced years, and that is His saying: ﴿When he reached his full strength and became mature, We gave him judgment and knowledge. Thus do We reward the good-doers.﴾"

His saying: ﴿وَاسْتَوَىٰ﴾ (and became mature) means that his youth reached its end and settled, so that there was no further increase in his youthfulness.

It has also been said: he rose from the state of deficiency to the state of perfection.

(A subtle point)

Deal gently with the weak; when they grow strong, become stricter with them.

Order them to pray at seven and strike them for neglecting it at ten. Islam, in its beginning, was like a drop of sperm; it was content with the word of monotheism. When the soul was breathed into it, it needed nourishment, so prayer was prescribed. When it began to move, emigration became obligatory. When it grew strong, zakat became obligatory. When birth drew near, hajj became binding. When it appeared as a child, it crawled gently: ﴿Allah intends ease for you﴾. When it feared slipping and punishment, the good tidings came: ﴿Do not despair﴾. When it grew up, the tutor said: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾. When it reached its full strength and became mature, there came: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾.

(Benefit: Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow)

This is a discussion of "al-yawm" (today), "ams" (yesterday) and "ghad" (tomorrow), and the reason each word is specialized to its meaning.

Know that the day nearest to you is your present day, the one you are in. One says "fa'alta al-yawm" (you did it today): the general noun is mentioned and then made definite by the particle of previous reference (al-'ahd). Nothing is more known to you than your present day, so the word is directed to it. Its counterpart is "al-an" (now), from "an" (the present moment).

As for "ams" and "ghad": since each of them is connected to your today, a name was derived for each from the hour nearest to it. "Ams" (yesterday) was derived for the past day that meets the evening (al-masa'), since it is closer to your day than its morning, I mean the morning of tomorrow. So they said "ams."

Likewise "ghad" (tomorrow): the name was derived from "al-ghad" (the morning), which is closer to your day than its evening, I mean the evening of tomorrow.

Consider how they made "ams" indeclinable (mabni) and inflected "ghad" (declinable), because "ams" is formed from a past-tense verb, "amsa" (he became evening), and that is indeclinable. So they set "ams" on the pattern of the imperative of "amsa yumsi" (become evening).

As for "ghad," it was not derived from an indeclinable base, since it cannot be said that it is derived from "ghada" (to go in the morning) in the way that "ams" can be said to be from "amsa." The most that can be said is that it derives from "al-ghadw" and "al-ghadwa," and neither of these is indeclinable.

This reason is better than the grammarians' reason that "ams" is indeclinable because it contains the meaning of the definite article (al-lam), its original form being "al-ams." They said this because they say "amsu al-dabir" and describe it with the definite article, which shows that it is definite, and it cannot be definite except by presuming the article.

But this is first refuted by their saying "ghadu al-ati," which would then require, by applying their reasoning consistently, that "ghad" also be indeclinable.

Also, "ams" has taken the course of proper names. It is, and God knows best, in the position of "asmit" and "atriq," which are among the words that came in the imperative form as proper names for a place: a man says to his companion there "ismat" (be silent) when he is in that place. So "ismit" in place is like "ams" in time.

Perhaps it was derived from their saying "amsa bi-khayr" (he was in good state in the evening), "amsa ma'anaa" (he was with us in the evening) and the like. It may be objected: how can its proper-name status be claimed when it is so common? We say: its being a proper name is not like the proper name of Zayd or 'Amr, but like that of Usama, Dhu'ala, Barra and Fujar, and its category is that in which the genus is treated as the individual in a personal name.

If it is said: what then is the difference between it and the common noun (ism al-jins)?

It is said: this has baffled many grammarians, so that they made the difference between them merely verbal, saying its effect appears in not taking tanwin, in being described as definite, in its occurring as a circumstantial accusative (hal), and similar things, yet they did not perceive the secret of the difference between a word whose referent is one indefinite member of the genus, common among them, and a word for the absolute genus.

So here there are three matters, each followed by a status:

The first: a specific definite member of the genus, which has the personal proper name, like Zayd.

The second: one member of them, common within the genus and not definite, so it has the indefinite noun, like "asad" (a lion) as one of the lions.

The third: the genus conceived in the mind, applying to each of its individuals, and it has the genus-name (ʿalam al-jins), like Usama. The counterpart of this is "ams" in time, and for this reason it is described as definite. So attach yourself to this benefit, which you will not find in any of the books of these people.

Praise be to God, the Bestower, who grants by His bounty.

(Commentary on Surah 28, verse 47)

This shows that what their hands had put forward is the cause for the calamity coming upon them, and had it not been ugly, it would not have been a cause. But the befalling of the calamity was prevented because its condition was absent, namely the non-arrival of the Messenger to them. So when the Messenger came, the cause was established and the condition was fulfilled, and "evil of what they had done" befell them, and they were punished for the first and the last.

(Section)

God, exalted is He, informed that what their hands had put forward before the mission (ba'tha) is a cause for their being struck by the calamity. And that if He had afflicted them with what they deserve of that, they would have argued against Him, saying: "You did not send to us a messenger, nor did You send down to us a book." So He cut off this argument by sending the Messenger and sending down the Book, lest people have any argument against God after the messengers. This is explicit that their deeds before the mission were ugly, to the extent that they deserved to be struck by the calamity because of them. But He, glorified is He, does not punish except after sending the messengers. And this is the decisive word (fasl al-khitab).

The verification of the statement on this great principle is: ugliness is established for the act in itself, and God does not punish for it except after the establishment of the proof through the message. This subtle point is what escaped both the Mu'tazila and the Kullabiyya, so each group boasted over the other, because neither combined these two matters. The Kullabiyya boasted over the Mu'tazila by their affirming punishment before the sending of messengers, and their placing punishment upon mere rational ugliness. And they answered well in refuting that against them.

And the Mu'tazila boasted over them in their denial of rational goodness and ugliness altogether, and in making the absence of punishment before the mission a proof of the absence of ugliness and the equality of acts in themselves. And they answered well in refuting this against them.

So each group boasted over the other because of its denial of the truth.

As for one who follows this path that we have followed, there is no way for either of the two groups to refute his statement, nor to prevail over him at all. For he agrees with each group on the truth it holds, affirming it, and disagrees with them in their falsehood, rejecting it.

And you find beneath this address that Allah does not guide those who follow their desires. He, glory be to Him and exalted, made the sources of guidance two kinds with no third: either what the Messenger brought, or desire (al-hawa). Whoever follows one of them cannot follow the other. Satan circles the servant, seeking the point of entry; he finds no entrance to him and no path to him except through his desire. Therefore, the one who opposes his desire, Satan flees from his shadow. Opposing desire is only made possible by longing for Allah and His reward, and by fear of His veil and His punishment. He finds the sweetness of cure in opposing desire, for following it is the greatest disease and opposing it is the greatest cure.

It was said to Abu al-Qasim al-Junayd: "When do souls attain their wish?"

He said: "When their disease becomes their cure."

It was said to him: "And when does their disease become their cure?"

He said: "When they oppose their desire."

The meaning of his saying "their disease becomes their cure" is that their disease is desire, so when they oppose it, they are cured of it by opposing it.

It was also said that desire (hawa) is so named because it plunges its owner downward (yahwi bi-sahibihi) into the lowest of the low (asfal al-safilin). Desire is three-quarters humiliation (al-hawan), and it is the greatest road to the Fire, just as opposing it is the greatest road to the Garden.

Abu Dulaf al-Ijli said:

"Alas for a young man who has manners, whose desire overcomes his manners,
He comes to the base thing while knowing it, and so stains a reputation that was guarding his honor.
But when he returns to reason, his insight comes back, and he weeps over the time that desire stole from him."

Ibn al-Murtafiq al-Hudhali said:

"How is it that I see what I see, while a man's resolve comes to him and his desire overcomes it?
So he is blind to what he sees against himself, and he thinks the one who sees him does not see him."

God Almighty has praised those who turn away from idle talk when they hear it, saying: ﴿When they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say, "To us our deeds, and to you your deeds."﴾

And this verse, although its occasion of revelation was specific, its meaning is general, encompassing everyone who hears idle talk and turns away from it, and says to his companions, with his tongue or in his heart: "To us our deeds, and to you your deeds."

(Section: On the argument of some schools for this verse, that the children of polytheists are in Paradise)

They said: If He, glory be to Him, does not destroy the towns in this world and punish their people except for their wrongdoing, then how can He punish with everlasting torment in the Hereafter someone from whom no wrongdoing has proceeded? It cannot be said: just as He destroys him in this world as a consequence of his parents and others, so likewise He will cause him to enter the Fire as a consequence of them. This is because the calamities of this world, when they descend, do not single out only the wrongdoer, but strike the wrongdoer and others alike, and people are resurrected according to their intentions and their deeds, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict only those among you who have wronged.﴾ [al-Anfal: 25]

It is like the army that is swallowed up by the earth together, with the coerced and the discerning and others among them.

As for the punishment of the Hereafter, it is only for the wrongdoers specifically, and no one who has no sin at all is made to share in it.

And He, exalted is He, said about the Fire: ﴿Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, "Did no warner come to you?" They will say, "Yes, indeed, a warner came to us, but we denied him and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything.'"﴾

And He, exalted is He, said to Iblis: ﴿Surely I will fill Hell with you and with those among mankind who follow you, all together.﴾ [Sad: 85]

If it is filled with Iblis and his followers, where then will the one who did not follow him settle within it?

They said: Furthermore, the Qur'an is full of reports that entry into the Fire occurs only through deeds, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾ [al-Naml: 90], and His saying: ﴿And they will find what they did present there, and your Lord does not wrong anyone.﴾

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 28, verse 68 (part 1 of 4):

﴿And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses. They have no choice. Glory be to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him. And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they disclose.﴾

That is, He, glory be to Him, is the One who alone creates and chooses from among His creation, and this is the choosing (al-istiṣfā’) and selecting (al-ijtibā’). For this reason, the complete pause (al-waqf al-tāmm) is at His words "and chooses." Then He negated from them the choice they proposed by their own will, and that this is not up to them but to the All-Creating, the All-Knowing, who knows best the locations of choice and its places, not to one who says: ﴿Why was this Qur’an not sent down upon a great man from the two cities?﴾ He, glory be to Him, informed that He does not send the messengers according to their choice, and that human beings have no right to choose over Allah; rather, it is He who creates whatever He wills and chooses. Then He, glory be to Him, negated that they should have choice, just as they have no creation. Whoever claims that the word "mā" is the object of "yakhtār" has erred, for if this were the intended meaning, then "al-khīrah" would be in the accusative as the predicate of "kāna," and the meaning would not be sound: "they did not have choice in it," with the returning pronoun omitted. The returning pronoun here is governed by a preposition, and the relative pronoun is not governed by the same preposition. So if it were omitted along with the preposition, there would be no indication of it, and its omission is not permissible. Likewise, whoever says that choice (al-ikhtiyār) here means will (al-irādah), as the theologians (al-mutakallimūn) say that He, glory be to Him, is "the Chooser who acts by choice," has not understood the meaning of the verse, for this terminology (iṣṭilāḥ) is a later innovation of theirs, and the speech of Allah is not to be interpreted by it. Rather, the word "ikhtiyār" in the Qur’an corresponds to its meaning in the language, which is choosing one thing over another, and it implies the preference of that chosen thing, its specification, and its prioritization over others. This is a matter more specific than general will and volition.

Al-Jawharī said in al-Ṣiḥāḥ (the lexicon): "al-khīrah is the noun from your saying: khāra Allāhu laka fī hādhā al-amr (Allah chose for you in this matter). Also, al-khīrah: one says, Muḥammad is the chosen one (khīrat Allāh) of His creation; and khīrat Allāh (with the vowel sukūn) also. Al-ikhtiyār is al-istiṣfā’ (selecting). Likewise al-takhyīr and al-istikhārah are seeking choice; one says istakhara Allāh yakhir lak (seek Allah's choice, and He will choose for you). And khayyartuhu bayna al-shay’ayn: I delegated the choice to him." End of quotation.

This is the meaning of ikhtiyār in the language, and it is more specific than what the theologians have established. From this is His saying: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair.﴾ And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointment.﴾ That is, he chose from among them.

By this the answer to the question raised by the Qadariyyah (the Qadariyyah, an early group who denied divine predestination) becomes clear. They say regarding disbelief and sins: are they occurring by Allah's choice or not by His choice? If you say by His choice, then everything chosen is pleasing, chosen, and beloved, so they would be pleasing and beloved to Him. And if you say not by His choice, then they did not occur by His will and choice.

The answer to this is to say: What do you mean by choice? Is it the general choice in the terminology of the theologians, which is volition and will? Or do you mean the specific choice found in the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the speech of the Arabs? If you mean the first meaning, then they occur by His choice in this sense, but it is not permissible to apply that term to them, because the word ikhtiyār carries the meaning of selection and love. Rather, one should say they occur by His will and power. And if you mean choice in the sense of the Qur’an and the language of the Arabs, then they are not occurring by His choice in this sense, although they occur by His will.

(Section)

Know that Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, is the One who alone creates and chooses among the creatures. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And your Lord creates and chooses.﴾

The intended meaning of choice here is not the will to which the theologians point when they say He is the Chooser who acts by choice; that is, He, glory be to Him, is indeed so. Rather, the intended meaning of choice here is this: the selecting (al-ijtibā’) and the choosing (al-istiṣfā’). It is a choice after creation, whereas the general choice is a choice before creation. So the latter is more general and prior, and this is more specific and subsequent. It is a choice from among the created, whereas the former is a choice for the creation. The more correct of the two opinions is that the complete pause is at His words "and chooses." Then "they have no choice" is a negation, meaning: this choosing is not up to them, but rather to the Creator alone. Just as He alone creates, He alone chooses from among them. No one may create or choose besides Him. He, glory be to Him, is most knowing of the places of His choice, the loci of His good pleasure, and what is fit for choice from what is not. Nothing else shares with Him in this in any way.

Some who have no verification (taḥqīq) or attainment (taḥṣīl) of knowledge claimed that "mā" in His words ﴿mā kāna lahumu al-khīrah﴾ is a relative pronoun, and it is the object of "yakhtār," meaning: "and He chooses that which they have choice in." This is false for several reasons.

First: the relative clause would then be devoid of a returning pronoun, because "al-khīrah" is nominative as the subject of "kāna," and the predicate is "lahum," so the meaning would be: "and He chooses the matter which was the choice for them," and this construction is impossible.

If it is said: it can be corrected by having the returning pronoun omitted, and the sense would be: "and He chooses that in which they had choice," meaning "and He chooses the matter in whose choosing they had choice."

It is said: this is corrupt for another reason, namely that this is not one of the places where omitting the returning pronoun is permissible. It is only omitted when it is governed by a preposition, and the relative pronoun is governed by the same preposition with the meaning being identical, like His saying: ﴿He eats of what you eat from, and drinks of what you drink from.﴾ [al-Mu’minūn: 33] and its like. But it is not permissible to say: "the one I passed by came to me," or "I saw the one I desired," and the like.

Second: if this meaning were intended, then "al-khīrah" would be in the accusative and the verb of the relative clause would be occupied by a pronoun returning to the relative pronoun, so it would say: "and He chooses what they had as the choice," meaning "that which was itself the choice for them." No one has read it this way at all, even though this would have been the proper wording of the sentence under this assumption.

Third: Allah, glory be to Him, relates the disbelievers' proposal in choosing and their wish that the choice be theirs. Then He negates this from them, glory be to Him, and makes clear that He alone chooses, as He said: ﴿And they said: Why was this Qur’an not sent down upon a great man from the two cities? Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord? It is We who have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We have raised some of them above others in degrees, that some of them may take others in service. And the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 31-32]

He rebuked them for choosing over Him, and informed that this is not up to them, but to the One who distributed among them their livelihoods, which contain their provisions and the terms of their lifespans. Likewise, He is the One who distributes His bounty among the people of merit according to His knowledge of the places of choice and who is fit for it from who is not. He is the One who raised some of them above others in degrees and distributed among them their livelihoods and degrees of preference. He alone is the Divider of that, not anyone else. Likewise in this verse, He made clear His sole right to creating and choosing, and that He, glory be to Him, is most knowing of the places of His choice, as He said: ﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say: We will not believe until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of Allah. Allah knows best where to place His message.﴾ [al-An‘ām: 124]

That is, Allah knows best the place fit for His selection, His honor, and His specification with messengerhood and prophethood, rather than others.

Fourth: He exalted Himself, glory be to Him, above what their polytheism implied of their proposal and their choice, and so He said: ﴿They have no choice. Glory be to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾

Their polytheism did not entail affirming another creator besides Him, such that He had to exalt Himself above that. So reflect on this, for it is extremely subtle.

Fifth: This is similar to His saying in [al-Ḥajj: 73-76]: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it. And if the fly should steal from them a thing, they could not retrieve it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought. They have not appraised Allah with His true appraisal. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.﴾ Then He said: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing. He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and to Allah are returned all matters.﴾

This is similar to His saying in [al-Qaṣaṣ: 69]: ﴿And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they disclose.﴾

And it is similar to His saying in [al-An‘ām: 124]: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message.﴾ So in all of that He informed of His knowledge, which entails His specifying the loci of His choice with what He specified them with, because He knows that they are fit for it and not others. So reflect on the context of these verses, and you will find that it includes this meaning and goes beyond it. And Allah knows best.

Sixth: This verse is mentioned right after His saying: ﴿And on the day He calls to them and says: What was your response to the messengers? The information will be obscured from them that day, and they will not question one another. But as for one who repents and believes and does righteousness, it is expected that he will be among the successful. And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses.﴾

Just as He alone created them, He, glory be to Him, chose from among them those who repented, believed, and did righteousness. So they became His elite among His servants and His chosen ones from His creation. This choosing was in accordance with His wisdom and knowledge, glory be to Him, for those who are fit for it, not according to the choice or proposal of these polytheists. So glory be to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.

[Section: On mention of what Allah has chosen from His creatures]

[Choosing indicates His lordship, glory be to Him]

When you reflect on the conditions of this creation, you see that this choosing and specification within it indicates His lordship, exalted is He, and His oneness, and the perfection of His wisdom, knowledge, and power, and that He is Allah, there is no god but Him. There is no partner to Him who creates like His creating, chooses like His choosing, or governs like His governing. So this choosing, governing, and specifying, whose effect is witnessed in this world, is among the greatest signs of His lordship, the largest evidence of His oneness, the attributes of His perfection, and the truthfulness of His messengers. So we point out a little of it, which will serve as a reminder of what lies beyond it and as evidence for what is other than it.

Allah created the seven heavens and chose the highest of them, and made it the dwelling of the nearest of His angels, and specified it with nearness to His Throne (kursī) and His Throne (ʿarsh). He settled there whom He willed of His creation. So it has a distinction and excellence over the rest of the heavens, and it would suffice that it is near to Him, blessed and exalted is He.

This preference and specification, despite the equal substance of the heavens, is among the clearest proofs of His perfect power and wisdom, and that He creates what He wills and chooses.

From this is His preference, glory be to Him, of the Garden of Firdaws over the rest of the gardens, and its specification by making His Throne its ceiling. And in some reports: "Indeed Allah, glory be to Him, planted it with His own hand and chose it for His chosen ones from His creation."

From this is His choosing from among the angels those chosen above the rest of them, such as Jibrīl (Gabriel), Mīkāʾīl (Michael), and Isrāfīl (Raphael). The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "O Allah, Lord of Jibrīl, Mīkāʾīl, and Isrāfīl, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants concerning what they differed about. Guide me by Your permission to the truth in what they have differed about, for You guide whom You will to a straight path."

He mentioned these three angels for the perfection of their specialness, their chosenness, and their nearness to Allah, although there are many other angels in the heavens, and He named only these three. Jibrīl is the bearer of revelation by which the hearts and spirits live. Mīkāʾīl is the bearer of rain by which the earth, animals, and plants live. Isrāfīl is the bearer of the Trumpet, which, when he blows into it, by Allah's permission his blast will revive the dead and bring them out of their graves.

Likewise is His choosing, glory be to Him, of the prophets from the descendants of Adam, upon him and them be prayers and peace. They are one hundred and twenty-four thousand, and His choosing of the messengers from among them, who are three hundred and thirteen, according to the hadith of Abū Dharr narrated by Aḥmad and Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ. And His choosing of the Ulū al-ʿAzm (the steadfast messengers) from among them, who are five, mentioned in the surah of al-Aḥzāb and al-Shūrā in His saying: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 7], and He said: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and what We revealed to you and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: Establish the religion and do not be divided therein﴾ [al-Shūrā: 13].

And He chose from among them the two Friends (al-Khalīlān), Abraham and Muhammad, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon them both and their families.

From this is His choosing, glory be to Him, of the offspring of Ismāʿīl from the kinds of the children of Adam. Then He chose from them the Banū Kināna from Khuzayma, then He chose from the offspring of Kināna the Quraysh, then He chose from the Quraysh the Banū Hāshim, then He chose from the Banū Hāshim the master of the descendants of Adam, Muhammad (ﷺ).

And in this way He chose His Companions from among the worlds. From among them He chose the first foremost ones, and from among them He chose the people of Badr and the people of the Pledge of al-Ridwan. For them He chose the most complete of the religion, the best of the laws, and the purest, most wholesome and most virtuous of the morals.

He also chose his Ummah (ﷺ) over all the other nations, as is related in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad and elsewhere, from the hadith of Bahz ibn Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"You are the completion of seventy nations, you are the best of them and the most honoured of them before Allah."
Ali ibn al-Madini and Ahmad said: The hadith of Bahz ibn Hakim from his father from his grandfather is sahih (sound).

The effect of this choosing appears in their deeds, their morals, their monotheism, their ranks in Paradise, and their standing on the Plain of Judgment. They are above the people, on a hill overlooking them. In al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, eighty of them from this Ummah and forty from all the other nations." Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan hadith. As for what is in the Sahih from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri from the Prophet (ﷺ), in the hadith about the sending forth to the Fire: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise," and he did not add to that.

So either it is said: this (the eighty-rows report) is more sound, or it is said: the Prophet (ﷺ) hoped that his Ummah would be half of the people of Paradise, and then his Lord informed him: "They are eighty rows out of one hundred and twenty rows." There is then no contradiction between the two hadiths, and Allah knows best.

Among Allah's favouring of His Ummah and His choosing of it is that He gave it knowledge and forbearance (hilm) which He did not give to any other nation. In the Musnad of al-Bazzar and elsewhere, from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ) say: "Allah, exalted is He, said to Jesus son of Mary: 'I am going to raise up after you a nation who, if they are afflicted with what they love, will praise and thank, and if they are afflicted with what they dislike, will seek reward and be patient, and they have no forbearance and no knowledge.' He said: 'O my Lord, how is that, when they have no forbearance and no knowledge?' He said: 'I will give them of My forbearance and My knowledge.'"

[His choosing, glorified and exalted is He, of the places and lands, the best and most noble of them]
Among this is His choosing, glorified and exalted is He, of places and lands the best and most noble of them, which is the Sacred City (al-Balad al-Haram). He chose it for His Prophet (ﷺ), made it rites (manasik) for His servants, and made it obligatory upon them to come to it from near and far, from every deep mountain pass. They do not enter it except humbled, submissive, abased, with their heads uncovered, stripped of the garments of the people of this world. He made it a sanctuary (haram) and a place of security, in which no blood is to be shed, no tree is to be cut, nor is its game to be frightened, nor its grass cut, nor is its lost property to be picked up for keeping, but only for announcing it. He made the intention to go there an expiation for past sins, erasing burdens and removing wrongdoings. As in the Two Sahihs, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever comes to this House and does not commit obscenity or sin, returns as on the day his mother bore him." He did not make the reward for its visitor less than Paradise. In the Sunan, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Follow up the hajj and the 'umrah, for they remove poverty and sins as the bellows removes the impurity of iron, gold and silver, and the accepted hajj (hajj mabrur) has no reward but Paradise." In the Two Sahihs, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The 'umrah to 'umrah is an expiation for what is between them, and the accepted hajj has no reward but Paradise." So if the Secure City were not the best of His lands and the most beloved to Him and the land He chose, He would not have made its open spaces rites for His servants, obligated them to head to it, made that one of the most emphatic duties of Islam, and sworn by it in His Mighty Book in two places, when He said: ﴿And this secure city﴾ [al-Tin: 3], and He said: ﴿I swear by this city﴾ [al-Balad: 1]. There is no spot on the face of the earth that every able person is obliged to strive towards and to circumambulate the House within it other than it. There is no place on the face of the earth that it is prescribed to kiss and touch and in which sins and burdens are removed other than the Black Stone and the Yemeni Corner.

It is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that prayer in the Sacred Mosque is worth one hundred thousand prayers. In the Sunan of al-Nasa'i and the Musnad, with a sahih chain, from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers elsewhere, except the Sacred Mosque, and a prayer in the Sacred Mosque is better than a prayer in this mosque of mine by one hundred prayers." Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih.

This is clear that the Sacred Mosque is the best of the spots of the earth absolutely. For this reason, setting out to it is an obligation, while setting out to other places is recommended but not obligatory. In the Musnad, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, from Abdullah ibn Adi ibn al-Hamra', that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while standing on his mount at al-Hazwarah in Makkah, saying: "By Allah, you are indeed the best of Allah's lands and the most beloved of Allah's lands to Allah, and if I had not been driven out from you, I would not have left." Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih hadith.

Moreover, among its special features is that it is the qiblah for all the people of the earth; there is no qiblah on the face of the earth other than it. Among its special features too is that it is forbidden to face it or turn one's back to it when relieving oneself, unlike the rest of the places on earth. The soundest of the views on this question is that there is no difference in this between open country and built structures, for there are more than a dozen proofs of this that have been mentioned in another place, and the one who differentiates has nothing that can withstand them at all, along with their contradictions regarding the measure of open country and built structure. This is not the place to exhaust the arguments of both sides.

Among its special features too is that the Sacred Mosque is the first mosque placed on the earth, as in the Two Sahihs, from Abu Dhar, who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the first mosque placed on the earth? He said: 'The Sacred Mosque.' I said: 'Then which?' He said: 'The Aqsa Mosque.' I said: 'How long between them?' He said: 'Forty years.'" This hadith has caused confusion for whoever does not know its meaning, who said: It is known that Sulayman ibn Dawud is the one who built the Aqsa Mosque, and between him and Ibrahim there are more than a thousand years. This is from the ignorance of this speaker, for Sulayman's part in the Aqsa Mosque was only its renewal, not its foundation. The one who founded it was Ya'qub ibn Ishaq, peace and blessings be upon them and their families, after Ibrahim built the Ka'bah by this measure.

Among what indicates its excellence is that Allah, exalted is He, informed that it is the Mother of Cities (Umm al-Qura). All other cities are subordinate to it and branches of it, and it is the root of cities, so there must be no equal to it among cities. Thus, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) described al-Fatihah as the Mother of the Qur'an, so it is the Mother of Cities, and for this reason it has no equal among the divine books.

Among its special features too is that it is not permitted for anyone other than those with recurring needs to enter it except in the state of ihram (ritual consecration). This is a special feature shared by no other land. This ruling was received by people from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them. It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, with a chain not used as proof, as a marfu' report: "No one enters Makkah except in ihram, whether from its people or not from its people." Abu Ahmad ibn Adi mentioned it, but al-Hajjaj ibn Artah is in its chain, and another before him among the weak narrators.

The jurists have three views on this question: negation, affirmation, and the distinction between one who is within the miqats (the boundary points) and one who is before them. So whoever is before them may not cross them except in ihram, and whoever is within them has the ruling of the people of Makkah. This is the view of Abu Hanifah, and the first two views are those of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad.

Among its special features too is that one is punished in it for intending evil deeds even if one does not commit them. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing, We will make him taste a painful punishment﴾ [al-Hajj: 25]. Consider how He used the preposition "bi" (with) after the verb "irada" (intend) here, and one does not say "aradtu bi kadha" (I intended with such-and-such) except where it is implied in the meaning of the verb "hamma" (to resolve), for one says "hammtu bi kadha" (I resolved upon such-and-such). So He threatened whoever resolves to do wrong therein with making him taste the painful punishment.

From this is the multiplication of the measures of evil deeds there, not their quantities. An evil deed is recompensed with an evil deed, but a great evil deed is recompensed with its like, and a small one with its like. The evil deed within the sanctuary of Allah, His land, and on His carpet is more emphatic and greater than it at one of the far edges of the earth. For this reason, one who disobeys the king on his own carpet of kingship is not like one who disobeys him in a distant place of his home and carpet. This is the decisive resolution of the dispute about the multiplication of evil deeds, and Allah knows best.

The secret of this preference and this special status has become apparent in the drawing of hearts, the yearning and inclination of souls, and their love for this Secure City. Its pull on hearts is greater than the pull of the magnet on iron. It is the most fitting for the saying of the poet:

*Its beauties are the raw material of every beauty,
and a magnet for the hearts of men.*

For this reason, Allah, glorified is He, informed that it is a *mathabah* (a place of return) for people, meaning they return to it through the passing of years from all regions, and they never have their fill of it, but rather, every time they visit it, their longing for it increases.

*The eye does not turn away from it when it looks at it,
until the eye returns to it longing.*

So, by Allah, how many slain, plundered and wounded are there for it, and how much wealth and souls have been spent in its love! The lover accepts separation from the dearest of his children, family, loved ones and homeland, placing before him all kinds of fears, perils, hardships and difficulties, yet he finds delight in all of that, takes pleasure in it, and considers it, if the authority of love has taken hold of his heart, sweeter than the blessings of the pampered and their comforts and pleasures.

*He is not a lover who counts his hardship
a torment, when his beloved is pleased.*

All of this is the secret of His attributing it to Himself, glorified and exalted is He, when He said: ﴿And purify My House﴾ [al-Hajj: 26]. This special attribution demanded from this honour, magnification and love what it demanded, just as His attributing His servant and messenger to Himself demanded from that the same. Likewise, His attributing His believing servants to Himself clothed them in majesty, love and dignity as it clothed them. Thus every thing that the Lord, exalted is He, attributes to Himself has a distinction and a special status over others, which necessitates for it election and selection. Then, by this attribution, He clothes it with another preference, a specialization and a majesty beyond what it had before the attribution. Whoever equated between essences, actions, times and places, and claimed that there is no distinction for any of them over any other, and that it is merely preference without a preferrer, has not been granted understanding of this meaning. This view is false, with more than forty aspects that have been mentioned in another place. It suffices to picture this false doctrine to see its corruption, for our position requires that the essences of the messengers be like the essences of their enemies in reality, and that preference is only by a matter that does not return to the particular essences being distinguished by attributes and virtues that do not belong to others. Likewise, the very places are one in essence; no spot has any superiority over another spot at all, but it is only because of the righteous deeds that occur in them. So there is no superiority of the spot of the House, the Sacred Mosque, Mina, Arafat, or the sacred sites over any spot of earth you name, and the preference is only with regard to a matter external to the spot that does not return to it or to an attribute that subsists in it. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has refuted this false view with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when a sign comes to them they say: We will not believe until we are given what the messengers of Allah were given﴾ [al-An'am: 124]. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124].

Meaning: not everyone is fit or suitable to bear His message. Rather, there are specific loci that are fitting for it alone and suitable for nothing else, and God knows best, among you, who is fit for these loci. Even if the essences were equal, as these people claim, that would not refute them. Likewise is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And thus We tried some of them by means of others, that they might say, "Are these the ones upon whom God has bestowed favor from among us?" Is God not most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [al-An'am: 53]

Meaning: He, glory be to Him, knows best who will be grateful for His blessing, so He singles that person out with His favor and bestows His grace upon him, rather than those who do not give thanks. Not every place is fit for His gratitude, for bearing His bounty, or for being singled out with His honor.

The essences He has chosen and preferred, whether among substances, places, persons, or others, comprise attributes and qualities subsisting in them that belong to no other. For these things God preferred them, and He, glory be to Him, is the One who gave them excellence through those attributes and singled them out for choice. This is His creation and this is His choice: ﴿And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses.﴾

How manifest is the falsehood of an opinion that holds that the site of the Sacred House is equal to all other sites, that the essence of the Black Stone is equal to all other stones of the earth, and that the essence of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is equal to the essence of anyone else. Preference in these matters is only due to matters external to the essence and to the attributes subsisting in it. These opinions and their like are among the transgressions committed by the theologians against the Shari'ah, which they attribute to it while it is innocent of them. They have nothing beyond the shared participation of essences in a general matter, and that does not necessitate their equality in reality, because things that differ may share a general matter while differing in their intrinsic attributes. God never equated the essence of musk with the essence of urine, nor the essence of water with the essence of fire. The clear disparity between noble places and their opposites, and between virtuous essences and their opposites, is far greater than this disparity. Between the essence of Moses (peace be upon him) and the essence of Pharaoh there is a disparity greater than that between musk and dung. Likewise the disparity between the Ka'bah itself and the house of a ruler is far greater than this disparity too. How then can the two places be made equal in reality, when the preference is by reason of what takes place there of acts of worship, remembrance, and supplications?!

We did not intend to exhaust the refutation of this rejected and despised doctrine; rather, we intended to portray it. Let the discerning, just, and rational person be the judge. God and His servants do not regard anything else at all. God, glory be to Him, does not single out anything, nor prefer it or give it precedence, except for a meaning that necessitates its singling out and preference. Indeed, He is the giver of that determining factor and its bestower. He is the One who created it, then chose it after its creation: ﴿And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses.﴾

[Section: On what God has chosen of deeds and other things]

The point is that God, glory be to Him and exalted, chose from every kind of created things the best of it, singled it out for Himself, and approved it over others. He, Exalted is He, is Good and loves only the good, and accepts from deeds, speech, and charity only the good. Thus the good of every thing is what He has chosen.

As for His creation, Exalted is He, it is general to both categories. By this one knows the sign of the servant's happiness and misery. The good is only suited to the good, is only pleased with the good, only dwells with it, and only his heart is at rest with it. So he has from speech the good word, which ascends to God, Exalted is He, only by it, and he is most averse to foul speech, vulgarity of tongue, obscenity, lying, backbiting, slander, slandering with falsehood, false speech, and every corrupt speech.

Likewise he only embraces the best of deeds, which are the deeds upon whose goodness sound natures and prophetic laws agree, and which sound intellects approve. Thus the Shari'ah, reason, and natural disposition agree on their goodness, such as worshipping God alone without associating anything with Him, preferring His pleasure over his own desire, drawing near to Him with all his effort and capacity, doing good to His creation as much as he can, so that he does to them what he loves they do to him, leaves them alone in what he loves they leave him alone in, advises them with what he advises himself, judges for them by what he loves to be judged for himself, bears their harm and does not impose his harm upon them, refrains from their honor and does not retaliate against them with what they have done to his honor, spreads their good when he sees it, conceals their evil when he sees it, and makes excuses for them as much as he can in matters that do not invalidate a law and do not contradict a command or prohibition from God.

He also has from character the best and purest of traits, such as forbearance, dignity, tranquility, mercy, patience, loyalty, gentleness of manner, softness of temperament, truthfulness, a heart free of rancor, deceit, spite, and envy, humility and lowering of the wing for the people of faith, might and severity against the enemies of God, guarding his face from humiliation and from abasing it before other than God, chastity, courage, generosity, and manliness, and every trait upon whose goodness the laws, natural dispositions, and intellects agree.

Likewise he chooses from foods only the best, which is lawful, wholesome, and digestible, nourishing body and soul in the best nourishment, with the servant being safe from its consequences.

Likewise he chooses from marriages only the best and purest, from fragrances only the best and purest, and from companions and associates only the good among them. So his spirit is good, his body is good, his character is good, his deed is good, his speech is good, his food is good, his drink is good, his clothing is good, his marriage is good, his entrance is good, his exit is good, his return is good, and his abode is all good. This is among those of whom God, Exalted, said: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are good, saying, "Peace be upon you; enter Paradise for what you used to do."﴾ [al-Nahl: 32]

And among those to whom the keepers of Paradise say: ﴿Peace be upon you, you have been good, so enter it, abiding eternally.﴾ [al-Zumar: 73] This fa' indicates causation, meaning: because of your goodness, enter it. God, Exalted, said: ﴿Corrupt words are for corrupt men, and corrupt men are for corrupt words; and good words are for good men, and good men are for good words.﴾ [al-Nur: 26]

The verse has been interpreted as meaning that corrupt words are for corrupt men and good words are for good men. It has also been interpreted as meaning that good women are for good men and corrupt women are for corrupt men. It encompasses that and more. Thus good words, deeds, and women belong to their suitable counterparts among the good, and corrupt words, deeds, and women belong to their suitable counterparts among the corrupt. God, glory be to Him and exalted, made all the good entirely in Paradise, and made all the corrupt entirely in the Fire. He made the abodes three: an abode purified for the good, which is forbidden to other than the good, and which has gathered every good, and that is Paradise. An abode purified for corruption and corrupt things, which none enters except the corrupt, and that is the Fire. And an abode in which the good and the corrupt are mixed and blended together, and that is this abode of ours. For this reason trial and affliction occurred because of this mixing and blending, in accordance with divine wisdom. When the day of the return of creation comes, God distinguishes the corrupt from the good, placing the good and its people in an abode apart, which no others mix with, and placing the corrupt and its people in a separate abode, which no others mix with. Thus the matter returns to only two abodes: Paradise, which is the abode of the good, and the Fire, which is the abode of the corrupt. God brings into being from the deeds of both groups their reward and punishment. He makes the good words, deeds, and characters of these people the very essence of their bliss and pleasures, and brings forth for them from these the most perfect causes of bliss and joy. He makes the corrupt words, deeds, and characters of the others the very essence of their torment and pains, and brings forth for them from these the greatest causes of punishment and pain, in consummate wisdom and overwhelming, dominating might, so that He shows His servants the perfection of His lordship, the perfection of His wisdom, knowledge, justice, and mercy, and so that His enemies know that they were the liars and fabricators, not His noble, truthful messengers. God, Exalted, said: ﴿And they swore by God their strongest oaths that God will not resurrect those who die. Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him, but most of the people do not know. [He will resurrect them] to make clear for them that about which they differed and so that those who disbelieved would know that they were liars.﴾ [al-Nahl: 38-39]

The point is that God, glory be to Him and exalted, made for happiness and wretchedness signs by which they are known. The happy, good person is only suited to the good, comes only with the good, issues only the good, and is associated only with the good. The wretched, corrupt person is only suited to the corrupt, comes only with the corrupt, issues only the corrupt, and is associated only with the corrupt. The corrupt man: corruption gushes from his heart onto his tongue and limbs, and the good man: goodness gushes from his heart onto his tongue and limbs.

It may be that a person has two substances, and whichever of them predominates over him, he is of its people. If God wants good for him, He purifies him of the corrupt substance before the encounter, so he meets Him on the Day of Resurrection purified, and does not need to be purified by the Fire, which He purifies him from through what He enables him of sincere repentance, effacing good deeds, and expiating calamities, until he meets God with no sin upon him. And He withholds from the other the materials of purification, so he meets Him on the Day of Resurrection with a corrupt substance and a good substance. God's wisdom refuses that anyone with his corruptions should dwell beside Him in His abode, so He causes him to enter the Fire for his purification, cleansing, and refining. When the ingot of his faith is freed from impurity, he becomes fit then for dwelling beside Him and living with the good among His servants.

The keeping of this kind of people in the Fire depends on how quickly those corruptions are removed from them or how slowly. The swiftest of them in removal and purification are the swiftest in coming out, and the slowest are the slowest in coming out: ﴿a recompense in accordance [with their deeds]﴾ [al-Naba': 26] ﴿and your Lord is not unjust to the servants﴾ [Fussilat: 46].

Since the polytheist is of corrupt origin and corrupt essence, the Fire does not purify his corruption. Indeed, if he came out of it he would return corrupt as he was, like a dog that enters the sea and then comes out of it. For this reason God forbade Paradise to the polytheist.

And since the believer who is good and makes others good is free of corruptions, the Fire is forbidden to him, since there is nothing in him requiring his purification by it. Glory be to the One whose wisdom dazzles minds and intellects, and whose creatures' natures and intellects testify that He is the Wisest of the wise and Lord of the worlds; there is no god but He.

(Section)
Whoever abandons choice and management, hoping for an increase, or fearing a loss, or seeking health, or fleeing from sickness.

And know that Allah is powerful over everything, that He alone has sole choice and governance, that His management of His servant is better than the servant's management of himself, that He knows his welfare better than the servant does, is more capable than him of bringing it about and securing it, is more sincere toward the servant than he is toward himself, more merciful to him than he is to himself, and kinder to him than he is to himself. The servant should also know that he cannot advance one step ahead of His governance, nor fall one step behind it. There is no one who can precede His decree and destiny, and no one who can delay them.
